title: [Performance][ROCm] shared_expert_gate ([1, K] weight) misses every skinny-GEMM path and costs 13.7% of the decode step
body:
## Summary

On ROCm, `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` dispatches on `m = weight.shape[0]`. Its two skinny-GEMM branches cover `m > 8` (wvSplitK) and `m % 4 == 0` (LLMM1), so for `m <= 8` only `m ∈ {4, 8}` are covered — **`m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7}` falls through** to `torch.nn.functional.linear` → rocBLAS. (The `n` conditions also differ: wvSplitK takes `0 < n <= 5`, LLMM1 only `n == 1`.)

`m == 1` is not a rare shape. In transformers today, `self.shared_expert_gate = torch.nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, 1, bias=False)` — i.e. a `[1, hidden]` weight — appears in **`qwen2_moe`, `qwen3_next`, and `qwen3_5_moe`**, invoked once per layer per token to produce the scalar that gates the shared expert's contribution. (`qwen3_moe` and `qwen3_vl_moe` have no shared expert, so they are unaffected; `glm4_moe` has a shared expert but no gate.) Because `bias=False` there, `bias is None` always holds for this call.

For a `1×2048 @ 2048×1` product, rocBLAS selects `Cijk_Ailk_Bljk_BBS_BH_MT128x32x16_..._GSU1_...` — a **128×32 macro-tile with no split-K**. That is one workgroup on a 40-CU GPU serially walking `k=2048`: **~140 µs to move 4 KiB of weights**, against **~7.9 µs** for every width the skinny ladder does cover.

Measured on a Qwen3.5-MoE 35B-A3B (40 layers, hidden 2048, 256 experts, 8 active), batch-1 decode, gfx1151:

| | |
|---|---|
| cost per call | 137 µs |
| calls per decode step | 40 (one per layer) |
| **total** | **5.48 ms of a 40.06 ms step = 13.7%** |
| decode after fixing it | 40.06 → 34.79 ms/step, **24.53 → 28.32 tok/s (+15.5%)** |

## Environment

- gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo), ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0
- vLLM 0.27.1 (the same dispatch conditions are present on `main` today)
- `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` at its default (`True`)

## Where

`vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py`, in `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`:

```python
    if use_skinny:
        x_view = x.reshape(-1, x.size(-1)).contiguous()
        if m > 8 and 0 < n <= 5:                                     # m == 1 fails
            ...
        elif m % 4 == 0 and n == 1 and k <= 8192 and bias is None:   # 1 % 4 != 0, fails
            ...

    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_tgemm_enabled():
        ...
    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)   # <-- m == 1 lands here
```

Note `is_tgemm_enabled()` requires `on_gfx950()`, and `use_aiter_triton_gemm()` matches only a hardcoded shape whitelist, so on gfx11xx there is no other path to catch this.

## Reproducer

Standalone, no checkpoint needed. Part A needs only torch; Part B additionally needs vLLM: https://gist.github.com/wenis/ea2a42350797771304a2d8ea8c7848f7

Output on the environment above, **stock vLLM**, `--k 2048 --iters 200`:

```
device : AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics
torch  : 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0
shape  : x[1, 2048] @ w[m, 2048].T  (batch-1 decode), bfloat16

=== Part A: torch.nn.functional.linear (vLLM's fallback path) ===
   m    us/call     GiB/s   note
   1     141.17      0.03   <- shared_expert_gate; 4 KiB of weights
   2      37.45      0.20
   3      40.33      0.28
   4      37.82      0.40
   8      39.65      0.77
  12      38.00      1.20
  16      39.09      1.56
  32      40.12      3.04
  64      37.81      6.46

m=1 as a reduction (x * w).sum(-1) :     5.47 us
m=1 via F.linear                   :   141.17 us   (25.8x slower)

=== Part B: vLLM's rocm_unquantized_gemm dispatch ===
   m    us/call   expected path
   1     139.93   *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback ***
   2      37.16   *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback ***
   3      38.82   *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback ***
   4       7.90   LLMM1 (m % 4 == 0, n == 1)
   8       7.88   LLMM1 (m % 4 == 0, n == 1)
  12       7.99   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
  16       7.95   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
  32       8.01   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
  64       7.96   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
```

Two separate things show up here, and I think only the first is vLLM's to fix:

1. **The dispatch gap.** `m = 1` costs **139.93 µs** against **~7.9 µs** for every covered width — **17.7x** — while moving *less* data than any of them.
2. **rocBLAS is additionally pathological at `m == 1` specifically.** In Part A, which never touches vLLM's ladder, `m = 1` costs **141 µs** while `m ∈ {2, 3, 4, 8, ..., 64}` all sit at **37–40 µs**. So `m = 2` and `m = 3` miss the skinny ladder too, but cost ~3.7x less than `m = 1` does. The degenerate single-row output is its own kernel-selection problem, independent of vLLM.

## Attribution

The 137 µs in the table above was measured on the full model and then traced, not inferred from reading the guard:

1. vLLM's own torch profiler (`--profiler-config.profiler=torch`), 51 decode steps under representative serving flags with CUDA graphs **on**. Kernel `Cijk_..._MT128x32x16_..._GSU1` appeared at **137.5 µs × 39.2 calls/step**. An `--enforce-eager` run agreed at 137.06 µs × 40 calls, so it is not a graph-capture artifact.
2. Call-chain attribution on the eager trace resolved it to `aten::mm < aten::matmul < aten::linear < vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm < vllm::moe_forward_shared`.
3. Dispatch counts for the step were exactly **271 = 231 `wvSplitK` + 40 fallback**, with `LLMM1` never taken — i.e. exactly one linear per layer misses the ladder.
4. `shared_expert_gate.weight [1, 2048]` is the **only** 2-D weight in the model with `shape[0] == 1`, so the 40 fallbacks are fully accounted for.

## Proposed fix

A `[1, K]` weight is a dot product. Adding it as a third branch in the existing ladder:

```python
        elif m == 1:
            out = (x_view * weight.reshape(-1)).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
            if bias is not None:
                out = out + bias
            return out.reshape(*x.shape[:-1], weight.shape[0])
```

With that mounted over the container's copy, Part B's `m = 1` row goes **139.93 µs → 6.82 µs (20.5x)**, and every other row is unchanged within noise (7.88–8.08 µs). End-to-end on the model above: **+15.5% decode**, with the `Cijk` kernel gone from the profile entirely and `wvSplitK` untouched (17.58 vs 17.54 ms/step), i.e. nothing else moved.

The `bias is not None` arm is defensive only — transformers builds this layer with `bias=False`.

Relaxing the `LLMM1` branch to accept `m < 4` looks unattractive: it passes a hardcoded split factor of 4, and the `m % 4 == 0` guard appears to be a vectorization requirement. The patch deliberately fixes only `m == 1`; `m ∈ {2, 3, 5, 6, 7}` remain uncovered, and I have no model that exercises them, so I would rather not widen it speculatively. Happy to restructure however maintainers prefer.

## Numerics — please read before taking the patch as-is

**The output is not bitwise identical to `F.linear`, and the difference is not only summation order.**

`x_view * weight.reshape(-1)` is a bf16 × bf16 product, so **each of the K element products is rounded to bf16 before it is summed**. `F.linear` accumulates the products in fp32 without rounding the intermediates. `torch.sum` then accumulates those bf16 values in fp32, so the reduction step itself is fine — it is the elementwise product that loses precision the GEMM keeps.

Measured on random bf16 vectors at K=2048, max absolute difference was **3.1e-02 to 2.5e-01** across runs, on dot products of order ~45 — a small number of bf16 ulps, but a real and systematic difference rather than pure reordering.

If that matters, the safer formulation is to widen before multiplying:

```python
            out = (x_view.float() * weight.reshape(-1).float()).sum(-1, keepdim=True).to(x.dtype)
```

which should keep the fp32 intermediates the GEMM has. **I have not benchmarked that variant** — it adds two small casts to a 4 KiB operand, so I would expect it to stay far ahead of 140 µs, but I would not want that assumption in the patch without a maintainer confirming which trade-off is wanted. Padding `m` to 16 and slicing the result is a third option that would stay exact and keep it a GEMM.

For what it is worth on end-to-end behaviour with the bf16-product version applied: greedy decode matched the unpatched baseline for 794 of 1028 characters (~200 identical tokens) before diverging at a near-tie between two equally plausible continuations, and across 400 tool-calling benchmark problems there were **zero malformed tool calls**. That is evidence the patched model is healthy in absolute terms; it is **not** a controlled A/B, since I do not have an unpatched run of the same benchmark. A maintainer wanting a strict before/after should ask for one.

vLLM already selects different kernels by shape, so bitwise stability across shapes does not appear to be a property it currently guarantees — flagging it explicitly in case that changes which fix is preferred.

## Relationship to existing work on this call site

**#43187** proposes a Triton fusion for the *same* call site — collapsing the gate's skinny GEMM, sigmoid and broadcast-multiply into a single kernel, measured on MI355x. I believe the two are complementary rather than competing, because they attack different layers:

- #43187 removes **kernel-launch count and intermediate tensors** in `models/qwen2_moe.py`.
- This issue is that `layers/utils.py`'s dispatch ladder **never offers that GEMM a skinny path at all**, so it lands on a rocBLAS kernel measured at 17.7× the cost of the ones the ladder does select for neighbouring widths.

If #43187 lands, its fused kernel replaces this call site for the models it covers, and this fix still applies to every *other* `m == 1` linear reaching `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`. If it doesn't, this fix helps the call site on its own. Fixing the dispatch also makes the un-fused path a fairer baseline to measure a fusion against.

**#39280** (merged) added AITER Fused Shared Experts, which bypasses the call site at MoE-block level — but it is opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`, default `False`) and requires AITER. **#37800**, which would have enabled it by default on ROCm, was closed. So on a default ROCm configuration, and on any configuration running with AITER off (as gfx1151 is here), the unfused path is what executes.

## Related

- #15830 introduced this dispatch (and, per its history, the `n <= 5` bound for spec decode).
- Point 2 under the reproducer may deserve a separate rocBLAS/hipBLASLt report: selecting a 128×32 tile with `GSU1` for a degenerate 1-row output is a poor heuristic regardless of what vLLM hands it.

title: [RFC]: Asymmetric P/D Deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash
body:
## Summary. DeepSeek-V4.1's bounded-replay structure creates an opportunity to make Prefill/Decode disaggregation substantially more asymmetric. Today, a Prefill worker still loads the full 40-layer model even though, after layer 20, only the final 128 prompt tokens need to be processed. This keeps almost half of the model weights resident on P for a small decoder-layer workload whose MoE utilization is likely poor. This RFC proposes moving that final 128-token window entirely to the Decode worker: - For a prompt of length `N`, P computes only `[0, N-128)` and transfers the resulting prefix KV state. - D computes `[N-128, N)` as its first full-model step and samples the first output token. - The request then continues through normal speculative decode with `q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens`. This asymmetry has two main benefits. - First, P would load only the causal encoder plus the minimal layer-20 KV/Indexer projection path, potentially removing close to half of its transformer-layer weights; a key target is fitting a production Prefill replica on one B300 GPU. - Second, moving the decoder-layer work to D increases the computational intensity of that work by executing it as part of D's much larger token batches, improving utilization relative to processing the 128-token replay on P. The execution model on D also becomes simpler than layer-local decoder replay. D never needs separate encoder and decoder token batches: ```text first D step: all L0-L39 process the same 128 prompt tokens later D steps: all L0-L39 process the same 1 + num_spec_tokens tokens ``` The trade-off is that each newly admitted request contributes 128 bounded-prefill tokens to a D step, which can temporarily increase the Decode token count and affect ITL (TPOT). This incremental cost is expected to be modest for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash: its light KV cache permits large Decode batches, and DSpark also makes each Decode batch process many tokens. Against that baseline, adding 128 tokens when a new request is admitted is a relatively small increase. This RFC is a design proposal for discussion. I do not currently plan to implement it, and there is no prototype or benchmark result yet. Implementation ownership is open. ## Proposed Change. ### Model placement and token ownership ```mermaid flowchart LR I[Prompt: N tokens] I -->|Prefix: N-W tokens| P I -->|Final window: W tokens| D subgraph P[Prefill worker: partial model] PE[Causal encoder L0-L19] PK[Minimal L20 Main-KV / Indexer
projection path] PE --> PK end subgraph D[Decode worker: full model] BR[First step: bounded prefill
L0-L39, q_len = W] FT[Sample first output token] ND[Later steps: speculative decode
L0-L39, q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens] BR --> FT --> ND end P -->|Prefix Main / Indexer KV| D ``` For prompts no longer than `W`, P performs no model forward and D processes the complete prompt. Conceptually, P would retain: - embeddings and complete layers L0-L19; - the minimal layer-20 projections needed to produce its canonical C1 Main KV and Indexer K; and - the state required by the KV connector handoff. P would not retain the complete layer-20 attention/MoE path, layers 21–39, final normalization, or the LM head. ### Request flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P as Prefill worker participant D as Decode worker P->>P: Run prompt prefix [0, N-W) P->>P: Produce prefix Main/Indexer KV P->>D: Send prefix KV D->>D: First step: run final W prompt tokens D->>D: Sample first output token D->>D: Later steps: normal speculative decode ``` Moving first-token generation to Decode is intentional. To minimize changes to the P-node scheduler, the P-node can compute the entire prompt (N tokens) instead of (N−W) tokens, since W is generally much smaller than N and the resulting redundant computation is negligible. ### Uniform Decode execution Decode has two full-model step shapes: ```text new request, first step: q_len = W active layers = L0-L39 later speculative decode steps: q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens active layers = L0-L39 ``` The first step is a bounded prefill using the transferred prefix state. After sampling, the request joins normal speculative decoding. This avoids changing the token set after layer 20. The attention history differs by cache group, but the query rows do not: - prefix-cacheable Main/Indexer groups read the transferred prefix state; - SWA groups are rebuilt locally over the replay window, following the mechanism in #56227; and - every layer executes the same `W` query rows in the first D step. If bounded-prefill requests and ongoing decode requests are scheduled together, their request-level `q_len` values differ. This step is a non-uniform batch and may fallback to piecewise cudagraph. ## Why This May Help. ### Smaller Prefill replicas Prefill node no longer needs the complete decoder stack or LM head. This is expected to remove close to **`half of the weights`** from each Prefill node. The exact saving depends on embeddings, KV pools, connector buffers, CUDA graphs, and allocator headroom. For DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, savings map straight to GPUs: tiny KV cache + offloading make Prefill HBM weight-bound, so halving transformer weights nearly halves the Prefill GPU count. A key target is fitting one production Prefill replica on a single B300 GPU. ### Avoid a low-density late-decoder tail on P The bounded replay contains at most 128 tokens per new request. Running it on P produces a small decoder-layer token workload and low arithmetic intensity because Prefill batchsize is usually small. In this proposal, D executes the final window as an ordinary full-model bounded-prefill step. It can batch multiple newly admitted requests and coordinate them with the larger Decode workload to get a **`higher arithmetic intensity`**. ### Simpler, unified model execution The split is by workers and token ranges, not by layer ranges within a forward: - P runs the entire model (encoder + layer-20 KV/Indexer projection path) on the prompt, using the same workload throughout each step—no workload reset between encoder and decoder layers. - D runs the entire model (encoder + decoder) on the bounded final window or normal decode workload. This makes the execution architecture **`simpler and more uniform`**, while naturally accommodating Chunked Prefill, Prefix Caching, and Context Parallelism. ### Cost and Trade-offs. The main cost is a larger first step on D: ```text new request, first step: q_len <= 128 later steps: q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens ``` Potential costs include: - D must support both bounded-prefill and speculative-decode shapes. - Admission bursts may increase ITL/TPOT for running requests. - Mixing both request types in one scheduler iteration may require piecewise CUDA graphs or eager fallback. This is likely **`acceptable`** for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash because its compressed KV cache permits a **`large Decode batch`**, and steps admitting new requests are usually a small fraction of all Decode steps. This requires measurement. ## Relationship to Existing vLLM Work. This proposal builds on, but is different from, two open vLLM PRs. ### #56227: encoder-side SWA bounded replay [#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227) already provides much of the required runtime behavior: - after a local or KV-connector prefix hit ending at `H`, the scheduler rewinds the final window; - the worker recomputes `[H-W, H)` locally; - Main/Indexer KV remains cached or transferred, while SWA is rebuilt locally; and - `Request.replay_start` and attention metadata floor the replay window. This PR is nearly orthogonal to the current RFC and provides sound logic for the P node's execution. ### #56752: decoder-side SWA bounded replay [#56752](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56752) compacts the batch after layer 20 so layers 21–39 process only each request's trailing window. That design still performs one forward in which different layer ranges process different token sets: ```text L0-L20: full prompt rows L21-L39: trailing W rows ``` This RFC proposes a different deployment boundary: ```text P: [0, N-W), L0-L19 and L20's KV/Indexer projection path D: [N-W, N), through all L0-L39 ``` Within a Decode step, every layer processes the same rows. There is no layer-20 compaction boundary, internal gather/scatter, or replay-layer sub-batch. ### Feedback Period. ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: finish_reason is "tool_calls" for a turn truncated at max_tokens, hiding the length stop from clients
body:
**Environment.** As in A.

**Describe the bug.** When a generation is cut off by `max_tokens` but any tool call was parsed, the response reports `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` rather than `"length"`. In `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py` the finish reason is computed as `auto_tools_called or (tool_choice == "required" and output.finish_reason == "stop")`, and `auto_tools_called` wins regardless of why generation stopped.

**Impact.** A client cannot tell a completed tool-calling turn from one guillotined mid-argument. Agent harnesses use `finish_reason` to decide whether to continue, retry with a larger budget, or execute; here they execute a call that may be the last complete one before the cut. It also silently corrupts any analysis that filters on the finish reason.

**Frequency.** 25 of 3,600 generations in our suite hit the cap exactly; each reported `tool_calls`. They were identifiable only by comparing `usage.completion_tokens` with the request's `max_tokens`.

**Suggested fix.** Let `length` win over the tool-call relabel, or surface the underlying stop reason alongside it.

AI assistance was used for the investigation and the measurement harness; I reviewed the findings and ran everything described here on my own hardware.

title: [Bug]: CUDA graph memory profiler charges an mnbt-linear profiling transient as "graph memory" → KV cache pool −18–24% on hybrid GDN models since v0.26.0 (the real FULL graphs cost ~24 MiB each)
body:
## Summary

Since v0.26.0, `profile_cudagraph_memory()` reports ~4.2 GiB of "CUDA graph
memory" on a hybrid-GDN model (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, int4 AutoRound, SM120) where
0.23.x reported 0.56 GiB for the *same graph set* (PIECEWISE=7, FULL=5). The
KV cache pool shrinks by the difference: **1,489,281 → 1,135,957 tokens
(−23.7%)** on 0.26.1 nightly, −17.9% on v0.26.0, with identical config.

Root cause (evidenced below): **~96% of the reported number is not graph
memory.** It is the allocator high-water mark of the estimator's *first FULL
sample*, the only sample that runs `profile_seq_lens =
min(max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens // num_tokens)` — a warmup+capture
whose total profiled context across the batch equals `max_num_batched_tokens`.
That forward transiently allocates **~128 KiB per batched context token** on
0.26.x (it did not on 0.23.x), and the measurement — a free-memory delta with
no `empty_cache()` between samples — charges the whole transient as CUDA
graph memory and sizes the KV pool down by it.

The real captures are innocent: with the new
`--profiler-config '{"capture_torch_profiler": true, ...}'` tracing, the
largest single allocation in any of the 12 real graph captures is **11.8
MiB**, and the estimator's own per-graph increments are 14–26 MiB.

⚠️ **A one-sided fix is dangerous** — see "Why this must be fixed as a pair"
below. On this model the mischarged 4 GiB currently doubles as activation
headroom that the memory profiler fails to attribute to the GDN long-prefill
path; releasing it to the KV pool (e.g. `cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE`, or
`VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`) produces a reproducible OOM
crash in `chunk_gated_delta_rule` on a single 32k prefill.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation (96 GB, SM120), TP=1
- Model: `Intel/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-int4-AutoRound` (hybrid: GDN linear-attn +

## Symptom

Identical config, boot logs:

| | 0.23.1 dev714 | v0.26.0 | 0.26.1rc1.dev245 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model loading | 62.61 GiB | 62.61 GiB | 62.82 GiB |
| CUDA graph memory (actual) | 0.56 GiB | 4.18 GiB | 4.19–4.21 GiB |
| Available KV cache memory | 18.74 GiB | 15.43 GiB | 14.31 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 1,489,281 tok | 1,223,338 (−17.9%) | **1,135,957 (−23.7%)** |
| Max concurrency @262,144 | 5.68x | 4.67x | 4.33x |

Graph set is identical in all three: PIECEWISE=7 (sizes 1–32), FULL=5
(sizes 1–16; capped by `max_num_seqs=16`). KV efficiency per GiB is unchanged
(≈79.3–79.5k tok/GiB) — the loss is purely "less memory handed to the pool".

## Evidence 1 — the estimator's own breakdown: it's one sample, not the graphs

`VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` on 0.26.1rc1.dev245:

```
Profiling CUDA graph memory: PIECEWISE=7 (largest=32), FULL=5 (largest=16)
Estimated PIECEWISE CUDA graph memory:  120.00 MiB first-capture + (7-1) × 14.00 MiB per-graph
Estimated FULL      CUDA graph memory: 4108.00 MiB first-capture + (5-1) × 24.00 MiB per-graph
Estimated CUDA graph memory: 4.19 GiB total
```

4,108 of 4,290 MiB is the FULL "first-capture" — the only sample where
`_warmup_and_capture` receives `profile_seq_lens` (gpu_model_runner.py, the
`mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL and i == 0` branch in `profile_cudagraph_memory`).
The FULL graphs themselves cost ~24 MiB each — same order as 0.23.x.

## Evidence 2 — it scales with max_num_batched_tokens, not max_model_len

Three boots of the same image, only the flagged knob changed:

| max-model-len | mnbt | FULL first-capture | total estimate | KV pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 262144 | 32768 | 4,108 MiB | 4.19 GiB | 1,135,957 |
| 131072 | 32768 | 4,108 MiB | 4.20 GiB | 1,031,329 |
| 131072 | 16384 | **2,070 MiB** | 2.12 GiB | 1,490,081 |

Exactly linear in mnbt (~128 KiB per batched context token), independent of
max_model_len. Consistent with `profile_seq_lens = mnbt // num_tokens` making
**total profiled context = num_reqs × (mnbt / num_reqs) = mnbt**. A separate
config on the same GPU with mnbt=2048 (NVFP4 sibling model) reports 0.61 GiB.

## Evidence 3 — capture traces: real captures allocate nothing big

`--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/traces","capture_torch_profiler":true}'`
traced all 12 real captures (trace for `capture_16_FULL` attached in a comment below; the other
11 available on request). Largest single allocation in ANY capture:
**11.8 MiB** (`aten::empty`); per-capture allocation totals 0.5–2.0 GiB of
small transients that the shared pool overlays across graphs. The real
capture path (`capture_model` → `_capture_cudagraphs`) never passes
`profile_seq_lens`.

The runtime "actual" figure is `start_free − end_free` spanning **all
warmups + captures + vision-encoder graph capture, measured before the
post-capture `empty_cache()`** — so warmup transients cached in the allocator
are counted as graph residency. Estimate and "actual" agree (0.4% diff)
because they mismeasure the same way, not because the graphs hold 4 GiB.

## Evidence 4 — the estimator didn't change; the model-side forward did

I diffed the two images file-by-file: `profile_cudagraph_memory`,
`_warmup_and_capture`, `profile_seq_lens` plumbing, `cuda_graph.py`
(pool sharing), `cudagraph_dispatcher.py`, and the GDN
`build_for_cudagraph_capture` are **byte-identical** between 0.23.1 dev714
and 0.26.1rc1.dev245 (modulo a ROCm stream fix and the new profiler hooks).
dev714 runs the same profile-seq-lens sample and reports 0.5 GiB.

So the ~128 KiB/context-token transient is a 0.23→0.26 regression in the
model-side decode-with-context path executed by that sample (the window
includes the FLA move to `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention`, the
`mamba/gdn/` package refactor, and new ops like `gather_initial_states`). I
did not pin the exact op: the capture profiler doesn't cover the estimator
phase. Wrapping `profile_cudagraph_memory()` with
`torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()` should name it in one run.

## Why this must be fixed as a pair (data from the v0.26.0 evaluation)

On v0.26.0 I tested the obvious mitigations:

- `cudagraph_capture_sizes: [1,2,4,8,16]`: 4.15 GiB — trimming graphs is not
  the lever (consistent with per-graph ≈ 24 MiB).
- `cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE`: reports 0.11 GiB, KV pool grows to 1,546,269 —
  and then the engine **OOM-crashes on a single 32k-token prefill**:

  ```
  vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/wy_fast.py, recompute_w_u_fwd
      w = k.new_empty(B, T, H, K)
  torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 458.00 MiB. GPU 0 ... 121.00 MiB free
  ```

- `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0`: same failure mode, silently.

The memory profiler measures peak activation at 8.29 GiB for this config, but
the real GDN chunked-prefill peak is ~4 GiB higher. The mischarged
"cudagraph" reservation currently absorbs that gap by accident. Therefore:

1. **Accounting fix** — don't charge profiling/warmup transients as CUDA
   graph memory (measure retained pool after `empty_cache()`, or isolate the
   profile-seq-lens sample from the graph-memory figure); **and**
2. **Profiling fix** — make the activation-peak profiling actually cover the
   hybrid (GDN) chunked-prefill worst case, so the freed memory is reserved
   for the reason it is actually needed.

Fixing (1) alone converts this from a −24% KV pool regression into an OOM
crash for GDN hybrids at long prefill. (3) Optionally, finding and removing
the new ~128 KiB/token allocation fixes the estimate at the source and
probably improves real decode-with-long-context memory behavior too.

## Reproduction

Any GDN hybrid at a non-trivial mnbt shows it; no load needed:

```bash
# boot with VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG and read the two
# "Estimated {PIECEWISE,FULL} CUDA graph memory" lines:
#   FULL first-capture ≈ 128 KiB × max_num_batched_tokens, per-graph ~24 MiB
# halve --max-num-batched-tokens → FULL first-capture halves, KV pool jumps
```

## Related

- #44740 — sibling defect in the same measurement (negative estimates on
  unified memory): both stem from free-memory deltas spanning warmup+capture
  with allocator caching in between; the open fixes there (#44745, #46932)
  address the sign error, not this transient mischarge.
- #30515 — the PR that introduced cudagraph memory profiling (the estimator
  logic itself is fine; it is measuring a forward that got 100× more
  allocation-hungry).

title: [Bug]: Whisper LLM.generate has no HF generate_with_fallback (loops / empty EOT)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text collect_env.py was not captured on the eval nodes. Experiment environment: vLLM 0.28.0 (Python LLM.generate). Also checked current main: LLM.generate still has no Whisper temperature fallback. OS: Linux (AMD EPYC CPU) Python: 3.13 Models: openai/whisper-large-v3, openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo, RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-quantized.w8a8, RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w8a8 Entry: Python LLM.generate + audio multi_modal_data (lmms-eval whisper_vllm) Dataset: LibriSpeech full (dev_clean / dev_other / test_clean / test_other) Sampling: temperature=0, max_tokens=256 Backends: stock vLLM CPU (no zentorch) and zentorch plugin — both loop / EOT ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `LLM.generate` for Whisper is a **single** greedy decode. HuggingFace `WhisperGenerationMixin.generate_with_fallback` retries a segment when zlib compression of the token ids is high (loop) or avg logprob is low. vLLM does not, so Python `LLM` callers (including lmms-eval `whisper_vllm`) can emit: 1. **Continuation loops** — the same clause for 200+ tokens (gzip 6–10). 2. **Empty completions** — immediate EOT, `token_ids=[]`. HF `_retrieve_compression_ratio` on empty bytes is `0.0`, so a naive port would **not** retry. vLLM often returns no tokens (EOS stripped); empty should be `needs_fallback` (`gzip = inf`). This is decoder stop / sampling, **not** a GEMM bug. It reproduces on **stock vLLM CPU Whisper** (no zentorch). zentorch plugin vs native WER gaps tracked which backend hit EOT first. `repetition_penalty` / `ignore_eos` / n-gram strip are the wrong fix. #### Related serving issue (different path — already filed) This is **not** a duplicate of the OpenAI transcription server bug: - Issue **#53144** — Whisper `/v1/audio/transcriptions` silently drops unread audio when the decoder EOTs inside a chunk. Still **open**. - PR **#53145** — recover abandoned stretch in **STT serving** (`speech_to_text`). Still **open**. - PR **#53236** — same serving bug; closed in favor of #53145. - Related: #58029 (`verbose_json` tail at chunk cuts), #25750 (Whisper feature tracking). #53144 / #53145 live in `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/`. This bug is **`LLM.generate`**, which lmms-eval actually calls. LibriSpeech clips are already <30 s, so serving chunk-carryover would not run even if #53145 merged. The two fixes are complementary: serving seek/tail vs Python generate gzip fallback. HF maps the same split: `generate_with_fallback` is gzip/logprob/temperature; unread-audio `seek` is `WhisperGenerationMixin` long-form (`_retrieve_segment`), not the inner `super().generate`. #### Repro (loop) ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams # Any Whisper checkpoint. Greedy, one generate — no HF temperature fallback. llm = LLM(model="openai/whisper-large-v3", max_model_len=448) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256) # LibriSpeech test_clean doc 1369 (and similar clips) can emit a 200+ word # n-gram loop, e.g. "i am a man of the law …" repeating, gzip ~6–10. # Native vLLM (no zentorch plugin) also loops (test_other 1279). prompt = { "prompt": "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>", "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio_array, 16000)}, } out = llm.generate([prompt], sp, use_tqdm=False)[0] print(len(out.outputs[0].text.split()), out.outputs[0].text[:200]) ``` Observed without fallback (lmms-eval LibriSpeech, vLLM 0.28.0): | Pair | Split | Result | |---|---|---| | large-v3 W8A8 | `test_clean` | RTOL **+21.3%**. zentorch plugin doc **1369**: ~250-word loop vs 23-word native | | same | `test_other` | native looped (~249 words, doc **1279**). Native WER 4.47 → 3.90 after fallback | | turbo BF16 | `test_other` | zentorch plugin looped on doc **238** (**+8.14%** RTOL) | With fallback (gzip > **1.35** or avg logprob < **−1.0**, retry T=0, 0.2, …, 1.0): - 1369 / 1279 / 238 loops gone; both backends same short hyp. - large-v3 BF16 zentorch plugin vs native RTOL: **+0.32 / −0.59 / −0.35 / −0.19%**. - Empty hyps retried only after empty `token_ids` → `needs_fallback` (e.g. `dev_other` 2037: 0 vs 7 words). HF `generation_whisper.py`: compression **1.35**, logprob **−1.0**, temperature list. HF AutoRun short-form + `return_timestamps=False` does not always enable that ladder; vLLM short-form still looped in practice. #### Proposed change (vLLM only) 1. `vllm/whisper_generation.py` — port HF `generate_with_fallback` / `_need_fallback` / `_retrieve_compression_ratio`. Empty `token_ids` → fallback. 2. Hook `LLM.generate` when arch is `WhisperForConditionalGeneration`. Inner calls `_whisper_inner=True`. Skip wrapper when `sampling_params` is a list (per-request `min_tokens`). 3. Unit tests, no GPU: gzip, empty ids, logprob, arch detect. Do **not** put this in `model_executor/models/whisper.py` (forward only). Not in this issue (need clip duration / extra generate / WER text — eval or serving #53145, not `LLM.generate`): - Duration-based `min_tokens` (~2 English w/s) - Unread-tail after last `<|t|>` (HF seek / serving #53145) - `tokenizer.normalize` for WER Optional later: `WhisperTimeStampLogitsProcessor` for timestamp prompts. Not fallback. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Qwen3 parser turns tool-call markup the model quotes into real tool calls (names outside request.tools, and duplicates of offered ones)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `v0.28.0` (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`), xgrammar 0.2.3
- Qwen3.8-27B, NVFP4 checkpoint; chat template sha256 `0a20a4673d45476ed88dcb4a60b6af35ca202ae470fee6fd2bd419758aabd9ab`
- `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'` (reproduced with and without speculation)
- RTX 5090 (sm_120), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming and non-streaming

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the model writes tool-call markup as *text* — quoting the format in its
reasoning, showing the caller an example, echoing the template's own
placeholder block — the `ParserEngine` transitions in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py`
(`(REASONING, TOOL_START)`, `(TOOL_BETWEEN, FUNC_PREFIX)`) fire on it, and the
response carries tool calls the model did not make. Two distinct classes:

1. **Names that are not in `request.tools`** — `function_name`, `...`,
   straight from the chat template's example block.
2. **Duplicates of an offered name** — the model shows a `get_weather` block
   and then makes the real call; the client receives two or three.

Both reach the client as ordinary `tool_calls`, so a harness executes them.

#### Minimal reproduction (parser-level, no server)

```python
from vllm.parser.qwen3 import Qwen3Parser
# tools = [get_weather(city: string)], thinking on
text = ("The format is:\n<tool_call>\n<function=function_name>\n<parameter=parameter_name>\nvalue\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>\nNow call it.\n</think>\n\n"
        "<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>\n<parameter=city>\nParis\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>")
# extract_tool_calls(text) ->
#   [('function_name', '{"parameter_name": "value"}'), ('get_weather', '{"city": "Paris"}')]
# streaming path: identical two calls
```

#### Measured on a live server

8 cases x thinking off/on x sync/stream, 100 repeats per cell, concurrency 4,
model-default sampling (T 1.0 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20), 3,200 requests per
arm, every failure carrying its raw generation. In ordinary cases the defect
is rare — 1-2 out-of-set phantoms per 1,600 thinking-on requests, the same
with speculative decoding on or off (it is the parser, not the drafter).

One prompt makes it the common case: *ask the model to show the tool-call
block it is about to use, then use it.* 100 repeats per cell:

| | unpatched 0.28.0 | with `validate_tool_names=True` (i.e. #50986) |
|---|---|---|
| out-of-set names (`function_name`, `...`) | **8** | **0** |
| duplicates of an offered name | 168 | 168 |
| legitimate calls withheld | — | **0** |
| pass, 800 requests | 393/800 | 421/800 |

Thinking on, 76-84 of every 100 responses to that prompt carry a duplicated
in-set call, in both arms.

### The fix for class 1 is already open: #50986

`ParserEngineConfig.validate_tool_names`
(`vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine_config.py:104`) gates `_emit_name_delta`,
`_handle_tool_end` and `extract_tool_calls` (`parser_engine.py:798, 858,
1033`), so a call whose name is not in `request.tools` is never emitted on
either path. `glm47_moe.py:179` opts in; `qwen3_config` does not. #50986
sets it. Measured on a deployed server, that PR:

- removes the out-of-set class outright (8 -> 0 above);
- **withholds nothing legitimate** — every `no_call` under the patch is a
  generation that emitted only placeholder markup; not one raw contained
  `<function=get_weather>`;
- leaves the #39056 implicit-end path (an offered call inside `<think>` with
  no `</think>`) parsing exactly as before — verified at parser level, sync
  and streaming.

### Class 2 is not covered by #50986, and only partly by #57553

Of 336 duplicate-call failures with raw generations kept:

- **86** contain a ``` fence — the shape [#57553](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57553) / #57541 addresses;
- **93** have a `<tool_call>` before `</think>`, i.e. quoted inside reasoning;
- the rest are unfenced quotations in ordinary content.

So fenced-example handling catches about a quarter of what we see. The
general case — the model showing the markup and then using it — needs the
parser to distinguish a quotation from an emission. Filing this so the two
classes are on the record separately; happy to supply raw generations for
either (fixtures are synthetic weather/file calls, nothing private).

Related: #39056 (opposite direction — calls inside `<think>` must not be
lost), #57541 / #57553 (fenced examples), #58105 (streaming loses calls when
the grammar admits ordinary-token delimiters), #54808 (`tool_choice`
`required`/named not enforced on chat completions for the XML parsers — a
grammar would have refused the out-of-set names).

AI assistance was used to investigate the code paths, build the measurement harness and draft this report; the human submitter reviewed it and ran everything described above on his own hardware.

title: [Bug]: CPU W4A16 Whisper fails: cpu_gemm_wna16 rejects 3-D encoder activations; packed k_proj bias is synthesized incorrectly
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cpu Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.15 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Aug 10 2026, 13:05:01) [GCC 14.4.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 384 Vendor ID: AuthenticAMD Model name: AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 96 Socket(s): 2 NUMA node(s): 2 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] numpy==2.4.6 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cpu [pip3] torchao==0.17.0+cpu [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cpu [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0+cpu [pip3] transformers==5.15.1 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [pip3] compressed-tensors==0.17.0 [pip3] vllm==0.27.1+cpu [pip3] zentorch==2.13.0.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: Could not collect ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Loading a compressed-tensors **W4A16 Whisper** checkpoint on **CPU** (`CPUWNA16LinearKernel` / `cpu_gemm_wna16`) fails at runtime. The Whisper encoder feeds **3-D** activations `[B, T, D]` into quantized Linear layers, but the C++ kernel treats the input as 2-D `[M, K]` and reads `K` from `input.size(1)`. For encoder time `T=28` that is not a multiple of 32, so the kernel aborts. Separately, packed checkpoints expose `.k_proj.weight_packed` and omit `.k_proj.bias`. `_create_fake_bias_for_k_proj` only matches `.k_proj.weight` and sizes the fake bias from `weight.size(0)`, which is wrong for packed AWQ/Marlin layouts (`d_model` is required). After the crash is avoided, that produces garbage transcripts (WER 100 on LibriSpeech in our runs). ### Repro Model: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16 ```python from vllm import LLM from vllm.assets.audio import AudioAsset llm = LLM( model="RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16", device="cpu", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=448, enforce_eager=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1}, ) prompt = "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>" audio, sr = AudioAsset("mary_had_lamb").audio_and_sample_rate outputs = llm.generate( { "prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, sr)}, } ) print(outputs[0].outputs[0].text) ``` ### Expected The request completes. BF16 openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo on the same CPU path is around 2.x WER on LibriSpeech; W4A16 should be in the same ballpark, not crash. ### Actual ```RuntimeError: Check failed: a_k_size % 32 == 0 (28 vs. 0)``` ### Root cause - 3-D activations. ops.cpu_gemm_wna16 does not flatten leading dims the way int4_scaled_mm_cpu already does (x.reshape(-1, x_shape[-1]), then reshape the output back). Whisper encoder Linear layers therefore pass [B, T, D] straight into the C++ op. - Packed k_proj bias. WhisperForConditionalGeneration.load_weights only walks .k_proj.weight. Compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoints use .k_proj.weight_packed and have no real .k_proj.bias. The fused qkv_proj/kv_proj path still needs a d_model-sized zeros bias; using packed dim0 is wrong. ### Suggested fix (native vLLM) - Flatten/reshape in cpu_gemm_wna16 to match int4_scaled_mm_cpu. - In _create_fake_bias_for_k_proj, also match .k_proj.weight_packed, size the fake bias from config.d_model, and do not override a real .k_proj.bias. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: FlashInfer autotune for trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe wedges forever on SM103 (GB300): trtllm_gemm cubin is sm_100a-only, no PTX, and the autotuner has no timeout
body:
> **EDIT (2026-09-23):** The root-cause attribution below is **withdrawn**. `nm -D` shows the `fp4_block_scale_moe` symbols live in `fused_moe_trtllm_sm100.so` (which carries `sm_103a` cubins), not `trtllm_gemm.so` (the dense GEMM module — the sm_100a-only observation is real but irrelevant to this op). The "candidate can never execute on SM103" mechanism does not hold. The symptom stands (unbounded autotune at boot, 40+ min, zero progress lines, no cache write before termination); it is now considered a probable extreme-slow-crawl rather than a proven hang, since the autotuner logs nothing between start and end and only writes the cache on completion. See [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58031#issuecomment-5788562400) for the corrected analysis and proposed scoping (exclude SM103 from `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` auto-selection; add per-bucket progress logging). The workaround below remains valid.

## Describe the bug

On a DGX Station GB300 (SM103, compute capability 10.3), the FlashInfer autotune for `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` runs indefinitely at 100% GPU with zero progress and zero autotune cache writes, wedging engine startup forever. There is no error, no traceback, no timeout — the boot simply never completes.

The root cause appears to be an arch-coverage gap in FlashInfer's prebuilt `trtllm_gemm` cubin, combined with an autotuner that has no timeout for a candidate kernel that never terminates.

## Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` pulled 2026-09-21 (vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev452+g3df4ae153`, FlashInfer `0.6.18.post1`), arm64
- GPU: NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), driver 610.43.02
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4 experts / MXFP8 rest), TP1, `--cpu-offload-gb 75`, DSpark speculative k=5
- Flags relevant: `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, moe backend auto-selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`

## Reproduction

Serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (or any model that routes MoE through `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`) on SM103 **without** skipping the op's autotune. Boot proceeds normally through weight load, CUDA graph capture, and JIT warmup, then reaches:

```
[flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:267] Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
[kernel_warmup.py:436] Using FlashInfer autotune cache file: .../autotune_configs.json
autotuner.py:972 - flashinfer.jit: [Autotuner]: Autotuning process starts ...
[kernel_warmup.py:358] Running FlashInfer autotune with 16384 tokens and token buckets (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536, 1792, 2048, 2560, 3072, 3584, 4096, 8192, 16384).
```

… and stays there. Observed: 40+ minutes at 100% GPU utilization, 0 new log lines in any 10-minute window, and the cache directory for the config hash created but left **empty**:

```
drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 Sep 21 15:35 .   # created when autotune started
# (no autotune_configs.json ever written)
```

By contrast, the JIT kernel warmup immediately before it completes with per-batch progress lines (10/10 batches in 47s), so the wedge is specific to this op's autotune, not to warmup in general.

The same behavior existed on the launch-day `deepseekv41-flash-0909` image, which is why this deployment has carried `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS="trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe,flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe"` since September 9. Reproducing it on current nightly shows the gap is not fixed.

## Root cause evidence

Inspecting FlashInfer's prebuilt cubins in the nightly image (`flashinfer_jit_cache`):

```console
# 907 .so files in flashinfer_jit_cache overall — sm_103a coverage exists:
$ for so in $(find . -name "*.so"); do cuobjdump -lelf $so 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "sm_103[a-z]?"; done | sort | uniq -c
   3380 sm_103a

# …but the cubin the fp4 block-scale MoE autotuner benchmarks:
$ cuobjdump -lelf .../jit_cache/trtllm_gemm/trtllm_gemm.so | grep -oE "sm_[0-9]+[a-z]?" | sort | uniq -c
      1 sm_100a

$ cuobjdump -ptx .../jit_cache/trtllm_gemm/trtllm_gemm.so | grep -oE "target sm_[0-9]+" | sort | uniq -c
      (empty — no PTX section at all)
```

`trtllm_gemm.so` ships **only an `sm_100a` cubin and no PTX**. An arch-specific (`a`-suffixed) cubin runs on exactly its target arch and never on a later one (this is the same mechanism as the `cooperative_topk` SM103 gap documented in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SM103 patch work — `sm_100a` cubins are unusable on SM103, and without PTX there is nothing to JIT forward).

So on SM103 the autotuner launches a candidate that either fails its launch silently or spins in a grid-stride loop sized for a different arch, and the `cudaEventSynchronize` in the timing loop blocks forever. The autotuner has no per-candidate timeout, so one non-terminating candidate wedges the whole boot.

## Suggested fixes (either would do; both would be robust)

1. **Ship an `sm_103a` (and ideally `sm_103`-JITable PTX) build of `trtllm_gemm`** — the rest of the JIT cache clearly builds for 103a (3,380 cubins), so this specific module looks like an omission rather than a fundamental limitation.
2. **Add a timeout to the FlashInfer autotuner per candidate/bucket** — a wedged candidate should be skipped and logged, not hang the engine forever. Right now one bad kernel costs an unbounded boot.

## Workaround

```
VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS="trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe,flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe"
```

With the skip, the same configuration boots to serving in ~8 minutes; the op then runs on its default (untuned) kernel selection. Measured decode on this deployment is ~91 tok/s single-stream with the skip in place.

## Additional context

- Full deployment config and the SM103 patch history: https://github.com/ebfio/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gb300
- The engine does not log *which* candidate config it was benchmarking when it wedged — if maintainers want a `py-spy dump` from a wedged process or a CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING run, I can reproduce the wedge on demand and capture it.

title: [Performance]: multimodal preprocessing is single-threaded per API server; a wider thread pool does not help (GIL) — process pool for _mm_executor?
body:
### Proposal to improve performance

**Summary.** For a VLM serving one image per request, the renderer's single-worker multimodal executor (`vllm/renderers/base.py`, `_mm_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`, "must stay single-worker per #38418") is a hard wall in front of the engine, and a wider *thread* pool barely moves it: with the cache disabled (so #38418 does not apply) I widened it on a B300 host — **2 threads: +20 % render throughput (14.0 → 16.8 pages/s); 6 threads: −70 % (→ 4 pages/s), GPU starved**. The GIL, not the cache, is the constraint. Proposal: run multimodal preprocessing in a **process pool**, sized by a config value, default 1 worker as today.

### Report of performance regression

Not a regression between versions — a measurement of the executor's shape at `v0.29.0`.

**Setup.** Qwen3.5-VL-class 4B model (custom weights), 1 × B300, 8 vCPU (Modal), `--max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-queued-reqs 216 --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}'`, `mm_processor_kwargs max_pixels=3145728`. Client: 300 simultaneous chat completions each carrying one inline 1275×1650 PNG (218 KB, ~2.1 k prompt tokens), `max_tokens = min_tokens = 1024`; then an open loop of 20 requests/s for 60 s with 16-token decodes, so the GPU drains faster than the render and the render alone sets the rate. "Pre-engine wait" is `time_to_first_token − time_in_model_prefill − time_in_queue` from the `llm_request` trace span (the time between `arrival_time` and the engine seeing the request — i.e. the renderer). A plugin replaced `_mm_executor` after `BaseRenderer.__init__` with a K-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor` (re-binding `_process_multimodal_async` / `_clear_mm_cache_async` via `make_async`) and set `set_default_torch_num_threads()`'s default to `8 // K` (also tried 8 per worker — same result).

| MM executor workers (torch intra-op threads each) | 300 at once: served p50 / p99 | pre-engine wait p50 / max | engine queue (`time_in_queue`) max | container CPU p50 (of 8 cores) | GPU util p50 | 20 rps × 60 s: pages/s served |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (8)** — today | 17.5 s / 28.5 s | 8.0 s / 14.5 s | 9.8 s | 1.4 (6.7 in the steady run) | 58 % | **14.0** |
| 2 (4) | 17.4 s / 28.3 s | 6.7 s / 11.7 s | 12.1 s | 1.4 (6.9 in the steady run) | 57 % | **16.8** (1200/1200 served, 0 refused; p50 8.8 s vs 13.3 s) |
| 6 (1) | **29.7 s / 57.1 s** | **27.3 s / 54.2 s** | **0** | 4.4 | 60 % | **4.2** |
| 6 (8) | — | — | 0 | 3.7 | 15 % | **3.8** |

Outputs at temperature 0 were byte-identical across configurations (30 requests, image by URL and inline); no errors or crashes in any configuration — thread-safety was not the problem.

**Reading.** Two threads help a little (the second thread overlaps the first's GIL-free tensor ops). With six render threads the engine's queue never forms and GPU utilisation drops: the renderer got *slower* in aggregate, and CPU utilisation fell rather than rose. That is the GIL-convoy signature: the HF processor's torch/numpy ops release and re-acquire the GIL per op, and with K render threads plus the event loop contending, every re-acquire waits a scheduling round, so a render that takes ~70 ms alone takes seconds abreast. The single worker's ~6.7 busy cores are its own intra-op threads (which is also why going from 8 to 16 vCPUs changed nothing for the single worker in an earlier run: the ops do not scale past ~8 threads).

**Why the cache guard is not the limit here.** #38418 (closing #38375) guards the multimodal processor *cache* — the LRU/SHM sender/receiver caches are not thread-safe and assume P0's insertion order at P1 — and #49524 kept `_mm_executor` single-worker for that reason. With `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`, `processor_cache_from_config` returns `None`, the engine core builds no receiver cache, and (with prefix caching off) `_process_mm_uuids` names every item per request; nothing is shared between requests. The remaining path is already thread-safe (`maybe_make_thread_pool`'s tokenizer copies, `AtomicCounter`). So a wider thread pool is *safe* in this configuration — it is just not faster.

**What would help.**
1. A `ProcessPoolExecutor` (or a small pool of forked/spawned preprocessing workers) for the CPU-bound part of `_process_multimodal`, sized by a config value (default 1 = today's behaviour), refused when the processor cache is enabled (the existing #38418 rule). The processed `MultiModalKwargs` would cross a process boundary once more (they already cross to the engine core), so the cost is one extra serialization of `pixel_values` per request — small against the ~70 ms render, and the GIL is per process.
2. Alternatively, `--api-server-count N` already parallelises renders across processes, but `--max-num-queued-reqs` / `--max-num-queued-tokens` are enforced per API-server process, so admission caps multiply by N; deployments that rely on those caps cannot use it as is. Making those caps global (or documenting the division) would make it a real option.

Happy to help test either on the same setup.

title: [Feature]: Bind batch-invariant mode into KV-offload namespaces and KV-connector compatibility checks
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Summary.** `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is not part of any KV-offload namespace or KV-connector compatibility check. An instance in batch-invariant mode can therefore load KV blocks that were produced under a different numerical configuration (non-invariant kernels, another attention backend, another GPU architecture) through a shared offload tier or a P/D transfer. Nothing signals that this happened. Its output then depends on whether a block was a hit and on which instance wrote it, which undercuts the documented promise that output is "deterministic and independent of the batch size or the order of requests in a batch".

This comes from reading the code at `v0.29.0` (98dff2a). **I have not reproduced a divergence.** I'm filing a feature request rather than a bug so it can be discussed before anyone builds a repro.

**What the code does today**

- The offload namespace is `FileMapper.fields`, which holds `model_name`, `tokens_per_hash`, `blocks_per_file`, the parallel sizes, `dtype`, `kv_cache_groups` and `inference_engine` ([file_mapper.py#L53-L64](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/v1/kv_offload/file_mapper.py#L53-L64)). The P2P tier's fingerprint is built from the same fields ([p2p/manager.py#L281-L286](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py#L281-L286)). The namespace has no batch-invariance flag, attention backend or device capability. The docs describe cross-instance sharing through a shared `root_dir` as working by default ([kv_offloading_usage.md#L155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md#L155)).
- The NIXL compatibility hash includes `attn_backend_name`, `cache_dtype`, `vllm_version` and more, but not the batch-invariance flag ([nixl/metadata.py#L171-L190](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py#L171-L190)). The other connectors I looked at (HF3FS, Mooncake, MoRIIO) have no model-level compatibility check.
- A grep for `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` or `batch_invariant` returns nothing under `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer`, `vllm/v1/kv_offload`, `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload` or `vllm/v1/core`. There's no warning of the kind `attention.py` emits when it disables prefix caching for FLASHINFER/TRITON_MLA under batch invariance ([attention.py#L363-L378](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py#L363-L378)).
- No test under `tests/v1/determinism/` configures a KV connector or an offload tier, so this combination isn't covered.

The same gaps are present on `main` today (88aa0d2).

**Why it matters.** The reason to enable batch invariance is reproducibility: RL rollouts versus the trainer, evals, and replay. Offload and P/D are exactly how those workloads get scaled out. A KV block written by a non-invariant producer is not the block the consumer would have computed. Recent namespace fixes such as #49438 (effective dtype) and #49440 (model runner / byte layout) close the gap for *interpretability*. This request is about *numerical provenance*, which matters only when a user has asked for determinism.

**Proposed change (small, opt-in by construction)**

1. **Offload namespace.** In `FileMapper`, add `"batch_invariant": True` to `fields` only when `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. That follows the pattern used for `replicated_layout`, where the field is written only when True, so existing deployments' digests are unchanged. When it is set, also add the attention backend name and the device capability, since batch-invariant bits are only reproducible within a backend and architecture. The P2P fingerprint picks this up automatically.
2. **NIXL.** Add the same factors to `compute_nixl_compatibility_hash`, again only when batch invariance is on, so mixed P/D pairs fail the handshake instead of silently mixing numerics.
3. **Connectors without a compatibility handshake.** Emit a `warning_once` when batch invariance is on and a KV connector is configured, mirroring the prefix-caching warning in `attention.py`.
4. **Docs.** Add a sentence to `batch_invariance.md` saying the guarantee covers KV transferred or offloaded only between producers with the same batch-invariance setting, backend and architecture.

I'm happy to send a PR for 1–3 if this direction looks right.

### Alternatives

- **Documentation only** (item 4). This is cheapest, but the failure stays silent.
- **Disable KV connectors under batch invariance**, as is done for prefix caching on FLASHINFER/TRITON_MLA. This is simpler but blocks the scale-out use cases above.
- **Namespace unconditionally** by backend and device. This is stricter, but it changes digests for every existing deployment and splits caches that are fine to share when determinism isn't required.

### Additional context

- The upstream offloading tests already acknowledge that the resume path isn't bit-exact for Mamba: the "not bit-exact" comment in [test_offloading_connector.py#L586-L590](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py#L586-L590). The GPU P/D accuracy tests use a 0.05 gsm8k tolerance. So nothing currently checks bitwise equality across a handoff under batch invariance.
- Related: #27433 (batch invariance tracking), #49261 and #49266 (model-revision namespace), #49438, #49440.

cc @orozery @ApostaC (kv_offload) @NickLucche (kv_transfer / NIXL) @yewentao256 (batch invariance). Sorry for the broad ping; I'm not sure which of you owns this intersection.

title: [RFC]: Adaptive Speculation Depth for MoE Models via Per-Iteration Utility Budgeting
body:
### Motivation.

Speculative decoding with a static `num_speculative_tokens` causes measurable
throughput **regressions** on MoE models (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-MoE, Kimi-K2,
Mixtral, etc.). This RFC proposes a lightweight, training-free, per-iteration
utility metric that dynamically adjusts speculation depth to prevent slowdowns
while preserving speedups when they are beneficial.

### The core problem: draft trees over-activate MoE experts

In dense LLMs, speculative decoding is reliably beneficial — the verifier
processes K draft tokens in a single forward pass at near-zero marginal cost.
For MoE models, this assumption breaks down.

A draft tree of K tokens collectively activates **many unique experts** across
the batch — often far more than K × top_k_experts — because different draft
tokens route to different experts. This causes:

1. **Expert weight bandwidth explosion** — each unique expert must be fetched from HBM
2. **EP all-to-all volume increase** — more unique destination ranks per step
3. **Verification time scaling with unique experts**, not just token count

Recent empirical results quantify this regression:

| Static K | Unique experts vs K=0 | Verification overhead | Net throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~1.3× | 1.1× | +10% |
| 4 | ~3.2× | 1.9× | −15% (slowdown) |
| 8 | ~6.1× | 2.4× | **−35% (severe slowdown)** |

The [Cascade paper (arXiv:2506.20675)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675)
implements an adaptive K controller in vLLM and shows that static K=4 causes
**up to 1.5× slowdown** on code/math workloads with DeepSeek-V3, while
adaptive K limits slowdown to 5% and yields **7–14% throughput improvement**
over the best static K choice.

This aligns directly with the Q2 2026 roadmap goal of
["composable speculation"](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39749)
and the active tracking issue
[#28947](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28947).

### Proposed Change.


### Core idea: per-iteration speculation utility as a dynamic K controller

Define **speculation utility** U at each decoding step as:

```
U = accepted_tokens_this_step / expert_activation_overhead_this_step
```

where:
- `accepted_tokens_this_step` — already tracked by the rejection sampler
- `expert_activation_overhead_this_step` — ratio of unique expert indices
  activated with speculation vs without; derived cheaply from the existing
  `topk_ids` tensor inside `FusedMoE.forward()` (zero additional compute)

**Control loop (test-and-set, no bandit, no training):**
- **Test phase** (short window, ~20 iterations): measure rolling U at current K
- **Set phase** (long, ~100 iterations): lock in K that maximized U
- If U < 1.0 for N consecutive steps → reduce K (or disable speculation)
- If U > threshold for M consecutive steps → restore K toward the configured max


### Codebase changes

**1. `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/` — `FusedMoE.forward()`**
Expose `unique_expert_count` as a side-channel output from the existing
`topk_ids` tensor:
```python
unique_expert_count = topk_ids.unique().numel()  # already computed, near-zero cost
```
This requires no new kernels and no change to the forward pass computation.

**2. `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` — new `MoESpecUtilityTracker` class**
```python
class MoESpecUtilityTracker:
    def update(self, accepted: int, unique_experts: int) -> None: ...
    def recommended_k(self, max_k: int) -> int: ...
    def reset(self) -> None: ...
```
Stateless across requests; operates on iteration-level aggregates.

**3. `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` — scheduler integration**
Wire `recommended_k()` into the step that sets `num_speculative_tokens` for
the next iteration. The adapted K is bounded by the user-configured max.

**4. `SpeculativeConfig` — new optional fields**
```python
moe_adaptive_spec: bool = False          # opt-in; no-op on dense models
moe_utility_threshold: float = 1.0      # U < threshold → reduce K
moe_utility_window: int = 20            # rolling window size (iterations)
```

**5. Telemetry (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py`)**
Add per-step logging of `spec_utility`, `active_k`, `unique_experts_activated`
for observability via existing Prometheus / W&B integration.

### What does NOT change
- Token acceptance logic (rejection sampler) — unchanged
- Draft model (EAGLE / MTP / n-gram / DFlash) — unchanged  
- Verification pass — unchanged
- Non-MoE models — the tracker is a no-op when no `FusedMoE` layer is present
- Existing `speculative_config` API — fully backward-compatible; new fields are optional

### Example API (no breaking change)
```python
llm = LLM(
    model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "mtp",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 4,   # upper bound; adapted downward at runtime
        "moe_adaptive_spec": True,
        "moe_utility_threshold": 1.0,
        "moe_utility_window": 20,
    },
)
```

### Open questions for discussion

1. **Where to compute `unique_expert_count`?** Preferred: inside
   `FusedMoE.forward()` from the existing `topk_ids` — zero overhead.
   Alternative: post-hoc from telemetry logs (higher latency, less useful).

2. **Discrete vs continuous K adaptation?** Cascade uses discrete
   K ∈ {0, 1, 2, 4}. Continuous adaptation (probabilistically drop the
   last speculative token) is possible but adds sampler complexity.

3. **Interaction with EPLB?** EPLB already rebalances experts across EP ranks.
   Should the utility metric count unique expert *ranks* rather than indices
   under wide-EP (e.g. 64-way EP for DeepSeek-V3)?

4. **Scheduler vs model-runner level?** The scheduler controls K for the next
   step; the model runner has `topk_ids` from the current step. A one-step
   feedback loop is simplest. Is this the right boundary?

5. **Interaction with MTP > 1 spec token for DeepSeek V3.2**
   (see [#31845](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31845)) —
   should adaptive K take priority over or compose with the MTP-specific
   per-model limits?

### Implementation plan (if RFC accepted)

- [ ] Add `unique_expert_count` instrumentation to `FusedMoE.forward()` (non-breaking)
- [ ] Implement `MoESpecUtilityTracker` with unit tests
- [ ] Wire `recommended_k()` into the spec-decode scheduler
- [ ] Add `moe_adaptive_spec` to `SpeculativeConfig` with documentation
- [ ] Benchmark on DeepSeek-V3 + MTP and Qwen3-MoE + EAGLE; report
  utility distributions and throughput vs static K baselines
- [ ] Gate behind flag, disabled by default, for safe rollout


### Feedback Period.

2 weeks

### CC List.

@benchislett  @mgoin  @fynnsu  @WoosukKwon @simon-mo

### Any Other Things.

### Prior art

| Work | Relevance |
|---|---|
| [Cascade (arXiv:2506.20675)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675) | Adaptive K in vLLM; 7–14% throughput gains on MoE |
| [MoE-Spec (arXiv:2602.16052)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16052) | Expert budgeting at verification time; training-free |
| [Tracking Issue #28947](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28947) | Spec-decode perf improvements (active) |
| [Q2 2026 Roadmap #39749](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39749) | "Composable speculation" roadmap item |
| [DDTree Feature Request #40809](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40809) | Related new drafting strategy |
| [RFC #45133 — Triton Kernel Dispatcher](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45133) | Related multi-platform kernel dispatch RFC |

The key distinction from the Cascade paper's external implementation is that
this RFC proposes integrating the utility controller **natively into vLLM's
scheduler and model runner**, rather than as a wrapper, making it composable
with async scheduling, EPLB, and all existing draft methods (MTP, EAGLE,
n-gram, DFlash) without modification.
